sec: Rumack-Matthew nomogram, King's College criteria and NAC protocol

items.q: Which graphic assessment tool is used to evaluate the severity of acetaminophen intoxication and determine the need for antidote therapy?
items.exp: The nomogram is titled 'Rumack Matthew Nomogram: Severity of acetaminophen intoxication'. (Book p996)

items.q: Match each axis of the Rumack-Matthew nomogram with the physiological parameter it plots — 1) X-axis 2) Y-axis … A) Plasma acetaminophen concentration (µg/mL and µmol/L) B) Hours after ingestion (from 0 to 24 hours)
items.exp: The X-axis plots hours after ingestion (0 to 24), and the Y-axis plots plasma acetaminophen concentration in µg/mL and µmol/L. (Book p996)

items.q: According to King's College Hospital criteria for acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure, what arterial pH cut-off is an independent indicator of poor prognosis?
opts: Arterial pH < 7.25 more than 24 hours after drug ingestion
Arterial pH < 7.35 within 12 hours of ingestion
Arterial pH < 7.10 within 4 hours of ingestion
items.exp: The first major criterion is 'Arterial pH < 7.25 more than 24 hours after drug ingestion'. (Book p996)

items.q: In the absence of arterial pH < 7.25, which of the following is NOT one of the King's College triad criteria for poor prognosis in acetaminophen ALF?
opts: Serum creatinine level > 3.4 mg/dL (300 µmol/L) or anuria
items.exp: The three concurrent King's College criteria are PT > 100 s (INR > 6.5), Creatinine > 3.4 mg/dL (300 µmol/L) or anuria, and Grade 3–4 encephalopathy; bilirubin is not part of this triad. (Book p996)

items.q: A patient presents within 4 hours of ingesting a massive acute overdose of paracetamol. What is the initial decontamination procedure indicated before antidote administration?
items.exp: For presentations < 4 hrs, the first treatment listed is 'Charcoal hemoperfusion'. (Book p996)

items.q: What is the drug of choice (DOC) for paracetamol overdose?
items.exp: N-acetyl Cysteine (NAC) is designated as 'DOC' for acetaminophen toxicity. (Book p996)

items.q: What post-ingestion deadline is recommended for optimal hepatoprotective efficacy when administering N-acetylcysteine (NAC)?
items.exp: The protocol states: 'Given within 15 hours'. (Book p996)

items.q: Match each infusion phase of the standard IV N-acetylcysteine protocol with its exact dose and duration — 1) Phase 1 2) Phase 2 3) Phase 3 … A) 100 mg/kg in 1 L of 5% Dextrose over the next 16 hours B) 150 mg/kg in 200 mL of 5% Dextrose over 15–60 minutes C) 50 mg/kg in 500 mL of 5% Dextrose over 4 hours
items.exp: The 3-stage infusion is: 1) 150 mg/kg in 200 mL 5% Dextrose over 15–60 min; 2) 50 mg/kg in 500 mL 5% Dextrose over 4 hr; 3) 100 mg/kg in 1 L 5% Dextrose over 16 hr. (Book p996)

items.q: Which oral sulfur-containing amino acid is listed as an alternative therapeutic option to N-acetylcysteine in paracetamol toxicity?
items.exp: Under treatment options, item c lists 'methionine'. (Book p996)

items.q: Assess the two statements on N-acetylcysteine: I N-acetylcysteine is also used therapeutically in non-acetaminophen drug-induced hepatotoxicity. II King's College criteria for poor prognosis in acetaminophen cases require both pH < 7.25 AND Grade 3 encephalopathy to be present together.
items.exp: Statement I is true because the note states NAC is used in other drug-induced hepatotoxicity. Statement II is false because pH < 7.25 is an independent predictor on its own; alternatively, all three other criteria must be present. (Book p996)

items.q: A 30-year-old woman is admitted 30 hours after an intentional acetaminophen overdose. Her arterial blood gas shows pH 7.21, serum creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, and INR 3.2. She is drowsy but conversant (Grade 1 encephalopathy). How does she meet the King's College poor prognosis criteria?
opts: She meets the independent criterion of arterial pH < 7.25 more than 24 hours post-ingestion
She meets the criteria because her INR exceeds 6.5
She meets the criteria because she has Grade 4 coma
She does not meet any poor prognosis criterion
items.exp: Arterial pH < 7.25 after 24 hours alone fulfills the King's College poor prognosis criteria, irrespective of encephalopathy grade or creatinine. (Book p996)
